purpose: Controlled inputs for original-application observation, not expected-output tests.

scenarios.name: baseline
scenarios.question: What defaults and objects exist after a minimal name/type import?

scenarios.name: name_patch
scenarios.question: Does a second import retain unspecified type and other state?

scenarios.name: repeat_file
scenarios.question: Does reimport update an existing object or create a new one?

scenarios.name: repeated_keywords
scenarios.question: Which values and mutations survive repeated definitions?

scenarios.name: name_before_type
scenarios.question: Can a name definition precede an object-type definition?

scenarios.name: unknown_keyword
scenarios.question: Does parsing continue after an unknown keyword line?

scenarios.name: invalid_numeric
scenarios.question: What state and parser status remain after an invalid numeric value?

scenarios.name: tetrahedron
scenarios.question: How are four coordinates and one tetrahedral connectivity row represented?

scenarios.name: relabelled_rows
scenarios.question: Do coordinate and element row labels determine storage positions?

scenarios.name: partial_coordinate_read
scenarios.question: Does a failed coordinate read roll back the previous arrays or preserve partial writes?

scenarios.name: sparse_object_id
scenarios.question: What objects and defaults fill gaps before a requested object ID?

scenarios.name: type_code_six
scenarios.question: Does type code 6 change an existing type?

scenarios.name: lowercase_keyword
scenarios.question: Are keyword names case sensitive, and does parsing continue?

limitations: The scenario recipes are questions; measured assertions live in tools/verify_keyword_observations.py.
Observed transcripts share state between imports; a scenario recipe is not itself evidence of an independently executed run.
These cases do not exercise materials, cross-object references, or command keywords.
Export may omit or transform incomplete objects; passive state probes are primary evidence.
